title: Kestrel and the Deadline
premise: Mirabel Marchetti, a hostage negotiator haunted by the crash of Flight 4471—a failure she was ordered to walk away from—has spent seven years as a ghost inside a security consultancy that quietly erases inconvenient people. When a transatlantic flight vanishes from every database mid-air, carrying a Russian cryptographer who claims he can prove 4471 was sabotaged, Mirabel is sent to extract him before his handlers silence him. She realizes the defector is bait, dangled to flush out anyone still asking questions about that night—including her. Choosing to stop running, Mirabel turns the extraction into a counter-trap, trading her own anonymity to expose the consultancy's director, and finally gives the victims' families the truth at the cost of the only life she had left.
about_author: Quentin Ishikawa is the pen name of a former aviation-industry analyst who spent a decade writing risk assessments before turning to fiction. He lives in coastal Oregon, where he writes about people who know exactly how systems fail because they helped build them.

chapters.title: The Board
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Seven years after Flight 4471, Mirabel talks a jumper off a bridge by phone while her firm's lawyers scrub the incident from public record. The routine success hollows her—the rules worked, but nothing was saved. Beat: competence as anesthesia; introduce her ritual of keeping one unsanctioned file on 4471 hidden in plain sight.

chapters.title: Ghost Altitude
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. A red-flag alert: Flight 9A to Reykjavik has vanished from every tracker while passengers are still texting from their seats. Her director, Calloway, assigns her a 'sensitivity consult'—extract passenger Anton Voss, a defector with a drive containing flight-manifest anomalies. Beat: dread; Mirabel recognizes the manifest format from 4471 and realizes this isn't coincidence.

chapters.title: Terminal Contact
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. In a Reykjavik transit lounge, Mirabel makes first contact with Voss, who refuses extraction unless she hears the recording: air-traffic audio proving 4471 received a stand-down order minutes before impact. Beat: vertigo of recognition; Voss knows her name, her old callsign 'Kestrel,' things no living person should know.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Mirabel and Voss. Voss explains he was the cryptographer who encrypted the stand-down order and kept a key; Mirabel tests his story against her own buried memories of that night's call. Meanwhile Calloway's instructions grow contradictory—first extract Voss, then 'assess for termination.' Beat: trust forming under duress; Mirabel understands Voss may be bait but follows anyway.

chapters.title: Cold Open
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. Flashback chapter: how Voss defected, what the consultancy's 'continuity division' does—erasing flights, witnesses, and negotiators who fail correctly. He reveals Mirabel wasn't reassigned after 4471; she was archived, a controlled asset. Beat: betrayal reframed; her seven years of invisibility were someone else's design.

chapters.title: Extraction Weather
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. The handoff at a harbor airstrip goes wrong: the extraction team is continuity division, and the plan is to burn both of them. Mirabel uses negotiation craft to split the team, buying escape into Reykjavik's storm-bound streets. Beat: survival instinct vs. the pull to finally fight; first blood, and no way back to her old life.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Hiding in a decommissioned air-traffic center, Mirabel decrypts Voss's drive fully: 4471 was downed deliberately to bury a whistleblower aboard, and Calloway signed it. She stops being prey—she drafts a negotiation plan where the counterpart is her own employer. Beat: transformation; the failure on the board becomes leverage.

chapters.title: The Stand-Down Order
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Mirabel engineers a fake extraction offer to lure Calloway's team, while Voss broadcasts fragments of the recording to force the firm's hand. Calloway counters by threatening the families of 4471's crew. Beat: rising tension at maximum; Mirabel must choose between exposing everything now or protecting the last innocent people in the pattern.

chapters.title: Final Approach
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Climax: face-to-face negotiation with Calloway aboard the same model of aircraft as 4471, parked and pressurized for the kill. Mirabel trades the only thing he wants—her silence and Voss's key—for a full confession recorded on the plane's own black-box-style logger. Beat: the negotiator takes herself hostage; she wins by refusing to survive invisibly.

chapters.title: Cleared to Land
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Aftermath: the recording reaches investigators and the families; Calloway falls, the consultancy fractures, and Voss disappears into a new life he chose. Mirabel testifies under her real name, ending seven years of ghosthood. Final beat: belonging purchased at the price of safety—and worth it; she keeps the bridge-jumper's thank-you note pinned above the file marked 4471, now closed.
